tasks.output:
S12 shipped on branch `charging-depth`, commit 4a1b4a0a.

Stop at window end: the planner records the window it auto-starts (persisted per vehicle), ends its charge-now override (`stopChargingOverride`) when that fixed end passes while the car is still drawing power, and clears the record on target/disconnect/stale windows. `ChargingPlannerDecisions.shouldStopChargingAtWindowEnd` holds the policy, including a one-hour grace so a late stop cannot interrupt a manual charge.

Sleep prevention: `SleepPrevention` wraps IOPMAssertion (`kIOPMAssertionTypePreventUserIdleSystemSleep`), driven through a `SleepPreventing` protocol. New `plannerKeepAwakeEnabled` defaults false and only acts with auto-start; the Settings → Automations toggle is disabled until auto-start is on, and both the caption and info button state that Hisingen cannot wake an already-sleeping Mac. The planner holds the assertion while a window is waiting or running and releases it when the target is met, the planner disarms, or Home Assistant owns the car.

Acceptance evidence:
- Plan stops at window end: unit decisions + controller tests (`aChargeStillRunningAtTheWindowEndIsStoppedOnce`, `theRecordedWindowEndDoesNotSlideWhileTheCarCharges`, deferred/refused stop handling).
- Opt-in, off by default, documented: `sleepPreventionIsOffByDefault`, `sleepPreventionHoldsTheAssertionWhileAWindowWaits`, settings-archive exclusion test, UI copy, docs/home-charging.md.
- Tests: 76 tests in 13 suites with `--filter ChargingPlanner`, plus 18 SettingsPreferenceTests; build with `-warnings-as-errors`; localization/l10n-usage/UI-discipline checks pass; 5 new strings translated in all 14 locales.

Changed paths: Sources/Hisingen/Services/Integration/{ChargingPlannerController,SleepPrevention}.swift, Domain/ElectricityPrices.swift, Services/Persistence/PreferencesStore+Charging.swift, App/AppDelegate{,+Automation}.swift, UI/Settings/{SettingsChargingPlannerCard,SettingsNavigation}.swift, all 15 Localizable.strings, Tests/HisingenTests/Unit/{ChargingPlannerControllerTests,ChargingPlannerTests,SettingsPreferenceTests}.swift, docs/home-charging.md, CHANGELOG.md.

Environment note: `Scripts/test.sh` here needs `SDKROOT` pinned to Xcode's MacOSX26.5.sdk because the Python 3.13 launcher injects the CommandLineTools SDK; that is unrelated to the change.

Open questions for integration: (1) if the slots after a stopped window are still the cheapest, the next tick may commit a new window — documented as a new plan rather than extending the old one; (2) sleep prevention holds while any window is ahead, which can be most of the day (documented) — it is not limited to plugged-in periods; (3) the only stop-like provider command is `stopChargingOverride` (resume schedule), which ends the planner's override but cannot override an active car schedule.

tasks.output:
Menu-bar quick controls for timers, OTA and charge locations are in the status item's menu on branch ui-l10n (commit 9f14b9d8), with all new strings translated in every locale and a 21-test model suite.

What shipped
- New `MenuBarQuickControls` model (UI/Shell) builds the rows from `ControlsCommandGate`: reported charging-window and cabin timers as pause/resume switches that preserve backendID/index/times/weekdays; OTA install-now, schedule in 2/8/12 h and cancel, using the card's own delays and state rules; per-saved-location optimised-charging switches; and a gate probe for "Save Current Location…". Rows that are temporarily blocked (busy, stale) stay visible and disabled with the gate's reason; permanently refused ones are omitted, matching the existing Actions-rotor rule.
- `StatusItemController` adds Timers, Software Updates and Charge Locations submenus after Quick Controls, plus the save-location NSAlert prompt. Every row is dispatched through `gate.send`, so the capability gate re-checks at press time. No status duplication: OTA appears only when an install/schedule/cancel action exists, timers only when the gate could allow one, and charge locations only when the feature is on.
- Keyboard: key equivalents on every new row while the menu is open (not global shortcuts, which DESIGN.md leaves undecided), standard NSMenu keyboard navigation, and the primary actions mirrored in the status item's VoiceOver Actions rotor (timer toggles, install/cancel, save location).
- Localization: three new keys (Timers, No timers reported., Save Current Location…) translated in 14 locales. "Timers" is allowlisted in Scripts/check-localization.py because Swedish and Dutch spell it identically; ratchet counts stay at the baseline.
- Changelog and docs/using-hisingen.md updated.

Verification
- `swift build` (fixture config, after `sh Scripts/inject-secrets.sh`): Build complete, 0 errors.
- `sh Scripts/test.sh --skip Live --no-parallel --filter MenuBarQuickControlsTests`: 21 tests passed.
- Adjacent suites (ControlsCommandGateTests, MenuBarGlyphTests, MenuBarIconStateTests, PanelPresentationTests, VehicleFeatureCompletionTests): 40 tests passed.
- `python3 Scripts/check-localization.py`, `node Scripts/verify-l10n-usage.mjs`, `node Scripts/verify-ui-discipline.mjs`: all pass.
- Full serial suite and a live app click-through were not run here; the menu surface itself is AppKit-only, which is why the decisions live in the tested model.

Notes for integration
- Build needs `HISINGEN_BUILD_CONFIGURATION=fixture sh Scripts/inject-secrets.sh` first, plus `SDKROOT=$(xcrun --sdk macosx --show-sdk-path)`; without SDKROOT the test script's manifest compile picks the CommandLineTools SDK and fails on this machine.
- The shared build lane was held by other sessions for ~20 minutes; I queued, then built after it freed. Other sessions were building without the lane at the same time, and the disk briefly hit 0 bytes free (it recovered).
- Antislop gate: PASS (no em dash in new copy, every row has real behavior or is disabled with a reason, keyboard and state coverage above, no fabricated content, DESIGN.md direction followed).
